stem: Which symptom pattern is most consistent with lactose intolerance?

options.text: Abdominal pain, diarrhoea, nausea, and flatulence
Isolated nocturnal bedwetting with a family history
Delayed meconium passage and abdominal distension from birth
Sacral dimple with reduced lower-limb reflexes
Soiling from overflow around a hard faecal mass

explanation: Abdominal pain, diarrhoea, nausea, and flatulence is the symptom pattern most consistent with lactose intolerance.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Lactose Intolerance

optionExplanations.A: Correct because abdominal pain, diarrhoea, nausea, and flatulence are typical gastrointestinal features of lactose intolerance.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because isolated nocturnal bedwetting suggests enuresis rather than lactose intolerance.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because delayed meconium passage and distension from birth suggest an obstructive bowel disorder such as Hirschsprung disease.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a sacral dimple with reduced lower-limb reflexes suggests a spinal abnormality, not lactose intolerance.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because overflow soiling around a hard faecal mass suggests constipation, not lactose intolerance.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
